title: Which Side Speaks, and How Sure?

scenes.visual: Title card: Which Side Speaks, and How Sure?.

scenes.tts: Language sits on the left in most people. But how most? And what does handedness tell you about one person?
scenes.visual: Two hemispheres side by side, the left one labelled: language, usually. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: Language sits on the left in most people. But how most? And what does handedness tell you about one person?

scenes.tts: One study measured healthy adults with ultrasound probes over each temple, while they generated words.
scenes.visual: A person with a probe at each temple, generating words. On screen only: functional transcranial Doppler, 326 healthy adults.
scenes.narration: One study measured healthy adults with ultrasound probes over each temple, while they generated words.

scenes.tts: The side whose blood flow rises more is scored as language-dominant.
scenes.visual: Two blood-flow traces, left and right. The left one rises more. Label: dominant.
scenes.narration: The side whose blood flow rises more is scored as language-dominant.

scenes.tts: Right-sided language appeared in about four of every hundred strong right-handers. It appeared in more than a quarter of strong left-handers.
scenes.visual: Three bars, numbers on screen only: strong right-handers 4%, ambidextrous 15%, strong left-handers 27%.
scenes.narration: Right-sided language appeared in about four of every hundred strong right-handers. It appeared in more than a quarter of strong left-handers.

scenes.tts: So most strong left-handers still speak with the left. Left-handedness raises the odds of right-sided language. It does not make it typical.
scenes.visual: The left-hander bar is split: 27% right-dominant, the rest left-dominant.
scenes.narration: So most strong left-handers still speak with the left. Left-handedness raises the odds of right-sided language. It does not make it typical.

scenes.tts: Now take equal numbers of strong right-handers and strong left-handers. Pick one right-dominant person. Is that person probably left-handed?
scenes.visual: An icon array: 100 blue dots for right-handers, 100 yellow dots for left-handers. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: Now take equal numbers of strong right-handers and strong left-handers. Pick one right-dominant person. Is that person probably left-handed?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: Yes. Most right-dominant people in this mix are left-handers.
scenes.visual: Right-dominant dots light up: 4 blue, 27 yellow. On screen only: 27 of 31, about 87%.
scenes.narration: Yes. Most right-dominant people in this mix are left-handers.

scenes.visual: The lit dots hold: 4 blue, 27 yellow, and 27 of 31, about 87%.

scenes.tts: Yet most left-handers are not right-dominant. These are two different questions.
scenes.visual: Beside the array: 27% of left-handers are right-dominant; the other 73% are lit as left-dominant.
scenes.narration: Yet most left-handers are not right-dominant. These are two different questions.

scenes.tts: Now change only the base rate, the share of each group. Make it nine right-handers in every ten. The rates stay the same.
scenes.caption: Now change only the base rate, the share of each group. Make it nine right-handers in every ten. The rates stay the same.
scenes.visual: The icon array becomes 1,000 dots, 90% blue and 10% yellow. The rates stay on screen.
scenes.narration: Now change only the base rate, the share of each group. Make it nine right-handers in every ten. The rates stay the same.

scenes.tts: Now fewer than half of the right-dominant people are left-handed. Right-handers are so many that they supply most of them.
scenes.visual: Right-dominant dots light: 36 blue, 27 yellow. On screen only: about 43% left-handed.
scenes.narration: Now fewer than half of the right-dominant people are left-handed. Right-handers are so many that they supply most of them.

scenes.tts: Same rates, different base rate, different answer.
scenes.visual: Card: same rates, different base rate, different answer.
scenes.narration: Same rates, different base rate, different answer.

scenes.tts: So for one person, handedness gives odds, not an answer. Before epilepsy surgery, the side of language has been tested directly.
scenes.visual: A patient before surgery; a question mark over each hemisphere resolves after a direct test.
scenes.narration: So for one person, handedness gives odds, not an answer. Before epilepsy surgery, the side of language has been tested directly.

scenes.tts: Which hemisphere speaks is a probability. Left-handedness shifts the odds without reversing them.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: a probability that shifts with handedness, but does not reverse.
scenes.narration: Which hemisphere speaks is a probability. Left-handedness shifts the odds without reversing them.
